result:
A race condition is a bug where the result depends on the unpredictable timing of two or more processes touching the same state. With a shared log, two writers can interleave partial lines or overwrite each other.

To avoid it, always open the log with `>>` and take a lock around the write with `flock`:

```sh
log=/var/log/app.log
(
  flock 9
  printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -Is)" "$msg" >>"$log"
) 9>"$log.lock"
```

`>>` opens the file with `O_APPEND`, so each write lands at the current end of the file. A single short `printf` or `echo` per line is therefore usually safe on a local filesystem even without the lock.

You need the lock when an entry spans several commands or lines, or when you read the file and then write based on what you read.

`flock` is advisory, so every writer must take the same lock. It can also be unreliable on NFS.
